scenarios.title: Local synthetic email session lifecycle — existing stored-data assertions
plannedActions: POST /auth/email/request synthetic address and proof challenge
POST /auth/email/request same address and proof during cooldown
POST /auth/email/verify incorrect code
POST /auth/email/verify correct code incorrect proof
POST /auth/email/verify correct code and proof
POST /auth/email/verify replay consumed code
GET /v1/me using issued session
GET /auth/sessions using issued session
POST /auth/email/request same synthetic account second device proof
POST /auth/email/verify second device proof and code
GET /auth/sessions with two authenticated devices
DELETE /auth/sessions second device from first device
GET /v1/me using revoked second session
GET /auth/sessions after second device revocation
POST /auth/logout using issued session
GET /v1/me using logged-out session

Read original identity/challenge rows after the original 16 HTTP actions; fixture only: seed one GitHub-style user with the boundary synthetic email as an unverified contact, no verified identity and no session.
Request a real local-mailbox challenge and validate exact row hashes, timing and zero identity/session mutation.
Submit a guaranteed wrong six-digit code with correct proof five times. After each exact 401, require attempts one through five and otherwise exact challenge and identity/session rows.
Submit the correct code and proof while still unexpired; require exact 401, attempts still five and no identity/session creation.
Request another challenge for the same email with a different PKCE proof. Dispatch two identical correct verification fetches before awaiting either, supplying an over-100-character device name.

Require exactly one 200 and one exact 401. Inspect one consumption marker and attempt, exactly one new user/identity/session, separation from the existing contact user, hashed token, device truncation and default expiry.
Read winning public identity and session list. Replay the identical verification and require exact 401 with full identity/session/challenge state unchanged.

Log out the winner, verify only its revocation timestamp changed, and require subsequent identity read 401. Preserve original rows and the locked/consumed challenge states, empty mailbox, 15 added requests and zero outbound attempts.
Read existing identity/challenge rows; reconfigure only the local mailbox fixture to accept then fail its first delivery response, and verify the same owned persistent state survives.
Send text/plain and foreign-origin JSON sign-in requests. Require exact errors, no mailbox attempt and unchanged identity/challenge/security-limit state.

Request a code with a fresh synthetic email/proof. The mailbox records the code then throws. Require exact sanitized 503, one failed challenge with nulled digest/send time and send_failed marker, and no new identity/session.
Retry immediately with the same email/proof. Require exact cooldown 429, unchanged failed challenge and no additional mailbox attempt.

Wait out the real one-minute cooldown without altering clock/storage. Request again with the same email/proof and require exact new challenge/code digest, bounded timestamps and replacement of the failed row.
Verify the successful replacement code/proof, check exact new user/identity/session/consumption rows, then read public identity.
Log out, require only bounded revocation of the new session, then require exact expired-session denial. Preserve all old rows, two send attempts, empty mailbox and zero outbound.
expectedOutcomes: Returns a challenge and expiry, and delivers exactly one synthetic mailbox code.

Each newly requested challenge has exact declared row shape, SHA-256 challenge ID and challenge-bound code hash, correct PKCE proof, zero attempts, null consumption, persisted sent timestamp and real ten-minute/one-minute expiry/resend values. Issuance creates no user, verified identity or session.

Five wrong codes each return exact 401/invalid_code, increment only the target challenge attempts by one through five, and preserve all users, verified identities and sessions. A correct code/proof while the challenge is still unexpired is then refused with attempts fixed at five, unchanged challenge row and no identity/session creation.

For the same synthetic email under a fresh distinct PKCE proof, two correct verification fetches are dispatched before either result is awaited. Exactly one returns 200 and one exact 401. The challenge has attempts one and one consumption marker; there is exactly one additional verified user, identity and session. A later identical verification is refused with all identity/session/challenge state unchanged. No particular internal transaction overlap is forced.

After real cooldown, the same email and PKCE proof replace the failed challenge with a new ID and exact new digest/timestamps/reset state, without increasing row count or changing other challenges. This exercises the production INSERT ON CONFLICT(email,pkce_challenge) replacement path; no concurrent resend is claimed.

Verification of the replacement code creates one exact email-namespace user with the returned ID, independently expected github_id/name/email/avatar_url and bounded creation time, plus exactly one verified email identity with the same user ID and verified_at equal to that creation time. Existing users and identities remain exact. No seeded contact user is credited as a verified identity.

scenarios.title: Synthetic GitHub OAuth and PKCE lifecycle — existing stored-data assertions
plannedActions: GET OAuth start malformed challenge
GET OAuth start valid challenge and client state
GET callback synthetic GitHub authorization
GET callback consumed state replay
POST exchange malformed verifier
POST exchange wrong valid verifier
POST exchange correct verifier after failures
POST exchange consumed code replay
GET identity using OAuth session
GET sessions using OAuth session
GET OAuth start cancellation fixture
GET callback provider cancellation
GET callback cancelled state replay
GET OAuth start token-error fixture
GET callback simulated token-error
GET callback token-error consumed state
GET OAuth start profile-error fixture
GET callback simulated profile-error
GET callback profile-error consumed state
GET OAuth start invalid-profile fixture
GET callback simulated invalid-profile
GET callback invalid-profile consumed state
POST logout OAuth session
GET identity after OAuth logout
Read original revoked user/session and empty OAuth state/code/verified-identity rows after the original 24 HTTP actions; fixture only: add one isolated unrelated user/session.
Start a fresh OAuth flow; observe the stored opaque-state hash, client state, fresh PKCE challenge and request-bounded ten-minute expiry without user/session writes.

Dispatch two identical callback fetches together. Require one redirect and one exact oauth_expired refusal, a single provider exchange, unchanged user/session rows and one correctly hashed two-minute exchange code.
Exchange the first code and proof once; require exactly one session for the existing user, exact token hash, requested device and default expiry.

Repeat with a second fresh state and proof for the same GitHub identity; after its callback dispatch two correct exchanges together and require one success and one invalid_code refusal with only one additional session.
List sessions using the second token and require exactly the two new active sessions. Attempt deletion of the unrelated session ID and require ok with complete declared auth state unchanged.
Read current identity, revoke the first session using the second, and check only the target timestamp changed. Require the first token refused and the second still able to list its sole session.

Log out the second session; require its token refused and only its revocation timestamp changed. Preserve original and unrelated rows, empty state/code/identity rows, 40 total HTTP requests, 14 simulated provider requests and zero denied outbound.
expectedOutcomes: Real starts store exactly one new OAuth state with the SHA-256 of the returned opaque state, distinct client state, correct fresh PKCE challenge and ten-minute expiry bounded by actual request time; users/sessions remain exact and auth codes empty.

Each successful callback consumes its OAuth state and stores exactly one two-minute exchange-code row containing the SHA-256 of the returned code, the existing user ID and the fresh proof challenge. No sessions are created until exchange.

Successful exchanges create one exact row each with independently hashed bearer, new session ID, existing user ID, named device, bounded created_at, default thirty-day expires_at and null revoked_at. Public sibling revocation and logout later change only the target revoked_at within request time; unrelated and original rows remain equal. This is persisted field behavior, not database uniqueness/nullability/cascade rejection.

plannedActions: POST /v1/teams with padded synthetic name
GET created team as owner
POST member invitation as owner
POST member invitation join while team is free
GET team after rejected free-plan join
Fixture only: seed active entitlement in owned D1
POST valid member invitation after fixture entitlement
POST same invitation again as existing member
GET team after duplicate member join
POST viewer invitation as owner
POST viewer invitation as viewer actor
POST viewer invitation as existing member
GET team as nonmanager member
POST invitation as nonmanager member
PATCH team name as nonmanager member
DELETE owner membership as owner
PATCH member role to admin as owner
GET team as newly appointed admin
PATCH team name as admin
GET viewer team list after rename
PATCH viewer to admin as admin
PATCH owner role as admin
POST team project as admin
GET project as viewer
PATCH viewer to member as admin
GET project after viewer promotion
DELETE project as ordinary member
DELETE own membership as ordinary member
GET own identity after leaving team
GET project after leaving team
DELETE viewer invitation as admin
GET team invitation list after revocation
POST revoked invitation as outsider
GET outsider identity after revoked join
DELETE admin membership as owner
GET team after owner removed admin
GET team as removed admin
DELETE team project as owner
GET owner project list after archive
GET archived project as owner

Read original membership/project rows; rejoin the member and viewer through the retained member invite, assign viewer role with owner PATCH, and create one new owner-held team project through public HTTP.

Seed each of seven entitlement tuples in turn: active/future-paid, trialing/future-paid, past_due/future-paid, active/recently-expired, canceled/recent-cancel plus old-paid, canceled/old-cancel plus recent-paid, active/old-paid without cancel.
For each tuple, GET the project as owner, member and viewer; check exact public project shape or exact 402. GET member identity; check project inclusion/omission and team role/status/plan.
In recent active expiry, attempt a fresh member project create; in old cancellation, attempt a fresh owner project create. Require exact 402 and complete declared business-state preservation.

After the last expired-grace tuple, list the existing project as owner, then archive it through the owner route. Observe only its archive/update timestamps change; owner listing becomes empty and direct lookup is 404.

Restore only the three fixture entitlement fields, leave both rejoined memberships through their own HTTP DELETEs, and read owner team. Preserve every original declared row exactly plus the one newly archived project; finish at 80 HTTP requests and zero outbound.
expectedOutcomes: Public creation returns the trimmed authored team name and the authenticated owner ID, and a following team GET returns the same team ID with exactly its owner membership. This checks persisted team identity/name/owner fields; it does not establish raw duplicate-ID or invalid-owner foreign-key rejection.
Entitled team admits a member through its valid invitation.

A public member invite join returns the expected team and member role; repeating that same invite as the same member still returns member and public team readback contains exactly one membership for that actor. No raw orphan-member insert or foreign-key cascade is asserted.
Promoted admin reads its persisted role, both invitations, and the unchanged original Synthetic team name after the denied member rename.
Admin creates a team project owned by the team owner.
Public manager readback marks only the selected invitation revoked.

After grace expires, the public owner DELETE archives the existing project. Read-only D1 comparison shows archived_at bounded by the request and updated_at equal to archived_at; all other project fields and business rows remain equal. Public listing becomes empty and direct lookup is 404. The three entitlement fixture fields receive no source credit.
